title: Intermittent throttle replay log - kai
content:
Summary:
This is a personal test log for a replay-style workload that intermittently hits the service with bursts that trigger our server-side throttle policy. Goal: understand how KV-cache, warmup penalties, and the throttle-replay backoff interact to produce tail latency spikes.

Hypothesis:
1) When bursts arrive after an idle window (>90s), KV-cache miss ramp + tokenizer overhead cause  p99 spikes.
2) Service throttle (token-based) coupled with jittered client retries amplifies tail events.
3) Warmup/cold-start cost is amplified for long-context requests (~1024 tokens) versus short ones.

Test environment (notes):
- Cluster: local dev pool (2x A10G), single model replica (gpt-small-ish, 8-bit quant).
- Runtime: serving v0.14.3+patch (PR 1882).
- Kernel: cudnn/12.1 tuned; nginx ingress removed to minimize extra queuing.
- Request runner: replayer v0.9 (custom), simulates production prefix distribution and cookie-based routing.
- KV-cache enabled: yes (prefix caching ON, capacity=64k entries).
- Throttle policy: token-bucket per-tenant, rate=80 req/s, burst=160, warmup_backoff=2s.

Workload specification:
- Duration: 30m runs each scenario.
- Patterns: (A) Bursty arrival: 5s high-intensity windows (peak 200 qps) every 30s.
            (B) Intermittent long-idle: 120s idle, then 20s burst at 120 qps.
            (C) Steady baseline: 60 qps continuous.
- Payloads: 60% short (<=64 tokens), 40% long (~1024 tokens).
- Retry policy (client): exponential jitter, max 3 retries, base 50ms.

Commands run (abridged):
- start replayer: ./replayer --pattern intermittent --duration 1800 --mix config.json
- capture metrics: prom-scrape -> local prometheus -> grafana snapshots saved

Observations (raw):
Scenario A (bursty every 30s):
- avg qps served (observed): 78
- p50: 32ms, p95: 210ms, p99: 1.82s
- error rate: 0.6% (mostly 429 from throttle)
- KV-cache hit-rate: 43% overall, but during initial 3s of burst drop to 12%
- GPU-util: jumps 28% -> 94% during burst, but sustained only 2.1s
- Noticed a cluster of p99s aligned with throttle 429s. Client retries create small spike waves that push more requests into the bucket and cause queueing.

Scenario B (long-idle replay):
- avg qps served: 54
- p50: 45ms, p95: 360ms, p99: 2.9s (worse than A)
- error rate: 1.9% (mix 429 + occasional 503 transient)
- KV-cache: cold at burst start; hit-rate initial 6% then increases to 50% after 8s
- Observed increased tokenization CPU at burst start (~70% CPU for tokenizer process)
- Conclusion: idle windows cause worst tail due to both KV-cache misses and tokenizer CPU saturation.

Scenario C (steady baseline):
- avg qps served: 60
- p50: 28ms, p95: 95ms, p99: 180ms
- KV-cache: steady 72% hit-rate
- GPU-util: steady 54%
- Minimal 429s, low retry amplification.

Latency timeline ASCII (snippet for scenario B p99):
Time (s)   p50   p95   p99
0-5        40ms  300ms 2.5s
6-10       35ms  210ms 1.1s
11-20      30ms  180ms 350ms

Key diagnoses: 
- KV-cache cold miss window is ~7-9s for long-prefix workloads; during that window GPU work + tokenizer CPU causes queues and triggers throttle.
- Throttle 429s are upstream of retry logic: client retries have jitter but aggregated retries form a microburst that keeps the bucket pegged.
- Warmup_backoff set to 2s gives some smoothing but insufficient for long-token requests where per-request GPU time is high (~1s).

Quick experiments attempted and outcomes:
1) Disable client retries: reduced p99 by ~300ms in scenario A, error rate rose but fewer cascading spikes.
2) Increase throttle burst to 300: smoothed 429s but increased p95 slightly; risk: fairness across tenants.
3) Pre-warm strategy: send low-cost prefix sweep during idle to populate KV-cache -> reduced cold-window from 8s to ~2s and p99 improved ~1.2s -> 600ms for scenario B.
4) Tokenizer process priority bump (nice -10): reduced tokenizer cpu spikes but risked starving other services; mixed results.

Actionable next steps / TODOs:
- (Short) Prototype background pre-warm job for idle tenants (opt-in). Measure costs vs tail improvement.
- (Medium) Tweak throttle policy to incorporate in-flight GPU latency estimate (not just req/s). Proposal: token-bucket credits scaled by estimated GPU-ms per-request.
- (Medium) Add server-side light retry suppression: when returning 429, include Retry-After and a short backoff token to avoid client retry amplification.
- (Long) Investigate tokenization offload (move tokenizer to separate CPU pool or dedicated microservice).

Notes to self / open questions:
- How often do production tenants have >90s idle windows? If common, pre-warm cost might be justified. Need usage histogram from analytics team.
- Potential safety: pre-warm could oppose billing model (customers pay for requests). Consider internal warm credits.
- Is KV-cache TTL tuned correctly for long-prefix workloads? Maybe increase capacity for tenants with high long-request ratio.

Raw metrics attached in snapshot: grafana-snapshot-id: graf-snap-2025-02-17-kr1 (linked in PR notes).

Wrap-up (one-line):
Intermittent replay bursts after long idle periods are the biggest tail-driver — KV-cache cold misses + tokenizer CPU + retry amplification produce multi-second p99s; pre-warming + smarter throttle policy appear to be highest ROI mitigations.

-- Kai
